metadata.title: Kyle Monangai is "Going to be OK," Deemed "Day-to-Day"
metadata.description: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson thinks that running back Kyle Monangai (thumb) is "going to be OK" and called his right-thumb injury a "day-to-day deal," according to Courtney Cronin of ESPN. Monangai stayed on the sideline for the end of the Week 4 win over the New York Jets on Sunday after suffering a thumb injury, but it does not appear to be much of a concern as the Bears head into their big Week 5 divisional clash at the Green Bay Packers this weekend. In the win over the Jets, Monangai had a huge workload, carrying the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns while also catching a four-yard pass as a receiver. The 24-year-old former seventh-rounder last year out of Rutgers already has two 100-yard rushing performances in his second NFL season through four weeks and has found the end zone three times on the ground. Monangai should be available against the Packers, and if he is, he will be a strong fantasy play against a Packers defense that has allowed 139.3 rushing yards per game, which is the fourth-highest in the league.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Day-to-day due to thumb issue
metadata.description: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said that Monangai is considered day-to-day after sustaining a right thumb injury in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
metadata.analysis: Monangai was on the bench for the final four minutes of the victory due to the injury, but he handled a hefty workload prior to his departure, finishing the day with 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns while tacking on a four-yard reception on his lone target. With imaging on Monangai's thumb revealing nothing overly concerning, Johnson is expecting the second-year back to be fine for next Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Even so, it wouldn't be surprising if Monangai ended up being a non-participant or limited participant when the Bears begin Week 5 prep Wednesday.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb) day-to-day
metadata.description: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said RB Kyle Monangai is day-to-day with his thumb injury.
metadata.analysis: Monangai is coming off a huge performance in Sunday's win over the Jets. His status will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb) to be evaluated Monday
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai (thumb) will be evaluated for a thumb injury on Monday.
metadata.analysis: According to the running back, he looked down at his hand before realizing any pain. His status is up in the air, so fantasy managers will need to monitor the situation as details emerge on whether he will miss time.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Awaiting Diagnosis on Thumb Injury
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (thumb) is awaiting more information after leaving late in Sunday's 23-12 win over the New York Jets. Courtney Cronin of ESPN reported that Monangai wasn't sure when the injury happened, only realizing at some point that his thumb was hurting. His final carry came with 4:08 remaining, and he did not return. Monangai still finished a huge afternoon with a career-high 30 carries for 146 yards and a career-best two rushing touchdowns, while adding one catch for four yards. He now has 324 rushing yards through four games after topping 100 yards twice already this season. The Bears were expected to get more clarity on the thumb Monday. Until that happens, there isn't enough information to know whether Monangai's Week 5 availability against Green Bay is in jeopardy.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai runs for 146 yards, two TDs in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for four yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Monangai dominated D'Andre Swift in the game as Swift lost a costly fumble and saw his playing time cut afterwards. Monangai rushed for touchdowns of one and five yards in the win. He will continue to split carries with Swift but it might be more of an even split after his Week 4 performance. He's on the flex radar in fantasy heading into Week 5 against the Packers.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Tending to thumb issue
metadata.description: Coach Ben Johnson said after Sunday's 23-12 win against the Jets that Monangai suffered a thumb injury during the contest, Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Monangai ripped off 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns to go with a four-yard catch on his only target in Week 4, while fellow RB D'Andre Swift notched 15 rushes himself for 58 yards and hauled in both of his targets for 16 yards. Perhaps the breakdown of RB touches among them is related to the knee injury that Swift tended to in advance of this game, but in any case Monangai now is dealing with a health concern of his own. The statuses of the two thus will bear monitoring as Chicago gears up for an NFC North road showdown with the Packers next Sunday.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai's Fantasy Value Jumps After Week 4 Breakout
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai just made this backfield much more interesting for fantasy managers. Monangai entered Sunday with exactly 10 carries in each of Chicago's first three games, then handled 30 of them for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the 23-12 win over the Jets. He scored from one yard out in the first quarter and found the end zone again from five yards in the third. The second score came after D'Andre Swift lost a fumble on Chicago's previous possession, and the Bears continued to lean heavily on Monangai the rest of the afternoon. Swift still had 15 carries for 58 yards, so this does not automatically make Monangai the unquestioned lead back going forward. It does make the split much harder to predict. Monangai matched his carry total from the first three weeks in one game and made the most of it, giving his fantasy value a significant boost coming out of Week 4.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai a Steady RB3 Against Staunch Jets Rush D
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai enters Sunday's home game against the New York Jets with low-end RB3/flex value in light of a tough matchup. Monangai and teammate D'Andre Swift have a stranglehold on Chicago's backfield, accounting for every running back rush attempt so far this season. While the former can't be trusted as a weekly high-upside fantasy play, a steady average of 11.3 opportunities (ten rushes) per game has kept him in the conversation. In Week 4, the second-year back out of Rutgers won't be afforded any favors in a Jets defense that's held opponents to a scant 87.3 yards per game on the ground. All that said, Monangai's involvement in a capable Bears offense and his ability to break off chunk gains should keep his fantasy value afloat until quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) returns. The New Jersey native is RotoBaller's PPR RB33 for the weekend ahead.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Not on the Week 4 Injury Report
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai is not on the team's Week 4 injury report and was able to practice in full on Wednesday. Monangai has nursed a knee injury in the early weeks of the season, but it has not kept him from playing in any of the first three games of 2026. The 24-year-old former seventh-round pick in 2025 from Rutgers has been impressive so far in his sophomore season while splitting the backfield with D'Andre Swift. He has 30 rushing attempts for 178 yards (5.9 yards per carry) and one rushing touchdown, while catching all four of his targets for 35 yards through the air. At the very least, the physical, big-play back should continue to be a strong RB3/flex option for fantasy managers, even with quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) likely to miss another game this weekend when the New York Jets visit on Sunday. Monangai has had exactly 10 rushing attempts in all three games so far this year, although he had just 31 rushing yards in Monday night's upset win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai rushes for 31 yards in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 10 times for 31 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3's Monday night game.
metadata.analysis: Monangai mixed in behind starter D'Andre Swift. He was held to 3.1 yards per carry by the Philadelphia defense in the contest while failing to find the end zone for the second straight game. Monangai will continue to see a modest workload for the Bears but he won't be a very strong fantasy option unless Swift were forced to miss time. He will now prepare to take on the Jets in Week 4.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Kept in check during win
metadata.description: Monangai rushed 10 times for 31 yards and wasn't targeted in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: The second-year back logged exactly half of D'Andre Swift's workload on the ground, with Monangai handling his third straight 10-carry total to open the season. The Rutgers product saw his efficiency take a notable dip for the second consecutive game following a stellar Week 1 where he averaged 10.0 yards per carry, yet Monangai's role as a fairly high-volume No. 2 back in Chicago's offense is safe. The lack of receiving work Monday night was a disappointment after Monangai posted a 4-35-0 line through the air in the first two games, but he'll have a chance to atone in what should be a favorable Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Remains a Low-End Flex
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai enters a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football without an injury designation. The former seventh-round pick was a DNP earlier in the week due to a knee injury, but he followed it with two full practice sessions. He should be good to go for his typical allotment of snaps against a formidable Eagles defense. Monangai handled 12 touches in each of Chicago's first two outings, cementing himself as a flex option with a solid weekly floor. However, he - and the entirety of the team's attack - will find tougher sledding in their first game without starting quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring). For now, it will be either Tyson Bagent (concussion) or Case Keenum getting the nod under center. Either option makes the offense more volatile, but it also seems likely the running game will get a bit more work in the process. Monangai remains in the flex tier for now - albeit a bit lower than previously - as RotoBaller's PPR RB37 for Week 3's contest.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Ready to Go for Week 3
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (knee) does not carry an injury designation for Monday night's game against Philadelphia. Monangai sat out Thursday's practice before returning as a full participant Friday, and he is no longer listed on the final injury report. The second-year back has gotten 12 touches in each of Chicago's first two games, rushing 20 times for 147 yards and a touchdown while adding four catches for 35 yards. He should be available to continue working alongside D'Andre Swift against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (knee) practices in full Friday
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Friday.
metadata.analysis: The young running back was able to return to practice in a full capacity on Friday after being absent on Thursday due to a knee issue of some kind. He should be a full go for Monday night's game but isn't expected to be a worthwhile fantasy option with Chicago likely to be down to their third-string quarterback for that matchup.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Logs full practice Friday
metadata.description: Monangai (knee) took part in Friday's practice and was listed as a full participant, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Monangai didn't participate at Thursday's session due to a knee injury, but his ability to get back to all activity one day later clears up the health of the running back ahead of Monday's game against the Eagles. Through two games this season while working in tandem with D'Andre Swift out of the Bears backfield, Monangai has racked up 182 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD on 24 touches.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Returns to a Full Practice Friday
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (knee) was back on the field Friday after being listed as a non-participant on Thursday's estimated injury report, according to Brad Biggs. The Bears did not practice Thursday, so that designation was only an estimate. Monangai also wasn't seen during the open portion of Wednesday's session. He has 24 touches for 182 scrimmage yards and one touchdown through two games, including 10 carries for 47 yards and two catches for 11 yards against Minnesota last week. Chicago still has another practice Saturday before issuing its final status for Monday night's game against Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (knee) doesn't practice Thursday
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai (knee) didn't take part in Chicago's practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Monangai missed Chicago's first practice of the week on Thursday. He's dealing with a knee injury right now and is considered day-to-day for the time being. It looks likely that he will be available to play on Monday night, though that is far from certain at this point.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - DNP on estimated injury report
metadata.description: Monangai (knee) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate.
metadata.analysis: Monangai dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 2 prep and now is tending to a knee injury as the Bears gear up for Monday's matchup with the Eagles. He'll have two more chances to mix back into drills Friday and Saturday, at which point Chicago could clear the air about his status. Through two games this season, Monangai has accrued 24 touches for 182 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Misses Practice on Thursday with Knee Injury
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (knee) was listed as a non-participant in his team's practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. The exact nature of Monangai's injury is not yet clear, but it appears as though the second-year running back's status for Chicago's Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football could be in doubt. Monangai has gotten off to a strong start to the 2026 season while splitting playing time with Bears RB1 D'Andre Swift, recording 182 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 24 touches across two games. Monangai missed time during training camp due to a hyperextended knee, so it's a little concerning for fantasy managers that he's now dealing with another knee issue. If Monangai is unable to play in Week 3, Swift could see a massive workload against Philadelphia on Monday.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Could See Expanded Role
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (undisclosed) was not seen at the portion of practice that was open to the media on Wednesday. Fantasy managers shouldn't be worried, with Monangai having plenty of time to get ready ahead of the Monday Night matchup versus the Philadelphia Eagles. The Bears are expected to be without quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) for at least a few weeks. Without Williams under center, the Bears are likely going to use a run-heavy offense featuring both Monangai and D'Andre Swift. During the first two games, Monangai has seen 10 carries per game, but he could see a larger workload going forward. The Bears passing game will be limited with Williams, so fantasy managers should expect to see a lot of Swift and Monangai.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Misses open portion of practice
metadata.description: Monangai (undisclosed) was not present during the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Monangai has been battling through multiple lower-body issues dating back to training camp, including a knee injury and a hamstring issue that limited him in practice last week. However, he has still been able to suit up and play well in both games so far. Saturday's injury report will be more telling for Monangai's status heading into Monday Night Football against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai not seen practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Bears RB Kyle Monangai was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The Bears are on a Monday Night Football schedule so the first injury report of the week comes out. Cronin notes that Monangai was in the injury tent in the second half against Minnesota.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai leads backfield in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai rushed 10 times for 47 yards while also catching both of his targets for 11 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Monangai struggled to make an impact against a strong Minnesota rushing defense, finishing with less than 50 rushing yards in the loss. The running back will look to get back on track in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Dozen touches in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Monangai carried the ball 10 times for 47 yards and caught both his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: The second-year RB led the Chicago backfield in rushing yards by two over D'Andre Swift on six fewer totes, but neither player was able to get into the end zone. Monangai has seen exactly 12 touches in each of the first two games of the season, turning that volume into 182 scrimmage yards and a rushing TD, but he could see more volume in Week 3 against the Eagles with Caleb Williams (hamstring) potentially unavailable, which would likely leave Tyson Bagent under center.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Offers Flex Appeal Vs. Vikings
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai offers solid standalone value in Week 2 despite a suboptimal outing against their division-rival Minnesota Vikings at home. Monangai's 10/100/1 box score in the team's thrashing of Carolina was strong output, though it's worth noting the second-year back was sparsely used early on. Regardless, he got it done for fantasy, and is positioned to run behind one of the league's better offensive fronts. While the 24-year-old's ceiling will be capped as long as he shares the backfield with running mate D'Andre Swift, he has enough athleticism and opportunity to make a fantasy impact. He'll land as RotoBaller's PPR RB33 for Sunday's appearance.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai - Will suit up Sunday
metadata.description: Monangai (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game versus the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Monangai and fellow RB D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) followed the same practice regimen this week, going from limited Wednesday and Thursday to all activity Friday. In the Bears' 59-37 win at Carolina this past Sunday, Monangai played second fiddle to Swift but still turned 12 touches into 124 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD on a 43 percent snap share, while Swift handled the other 57 percent and had 19 touches for 134 total yards and three rushing TDs.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Monangai is going to be good to go for Sunday's game, despite being limited at practice earlier in the week due to a hamstring injury. He shouldn't have any limitations and will likely continue to be an involved backup behind D'Andre Swift in this game and beyond.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai Cleared to Face Minnesota
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (hamstring) has been cleared to play Sunday against Minnesota, according to Adam Schefter. Monangai was limited Wednesday and Thursday after the hamstring issue landed him on the injury report, but he won't carry a game designation into the weekend. The second-year back made the most of his work in the opener, running 10 times for 100 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 24 yards. His biggest play was a 61-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter. Chicago still got Monangai 12 touches on a day when D'Andre Swift ran for 124 yards and three scores, giving the Bears two productive options coming out of Week 1.

metadata.title: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) was limited at Chicago's practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Monangai was again limited at practice due to a hamstring injury on Thursday. It doesn't seem like more than a minor issue at this point, however, so fantasy managers should expect Chicago's backfield splits to look normal in Week 2, assuming him and D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) are both cleared to play before game time.
